title: Notes Java Program Without And With Object Orientation

runs.text: 1. What are the four main pillars of object-oriented programming?
The four main pillars are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and
abstraction.
2. Why is it useful to demonstrate all four OOP pillars in one Java application?
It shows how the concepts work together in a practical program instead of explaining each concept only in isolation.
3. Which shapes are used in the area-calculat
ion application?
The application uses three shapes: Square, Rectangle, and Circle. It calculates and displays the area of each shape.
4. Why is a program that uses separate classes not automatically considered a complete object-oriented design?
Creating se
parate classes and objects is not enough by itself. A complete object-oriented design should also apply the relevant OOP concepts, such as encapsulation, inheritance, abstraction, and polymorphism.
5. What is clean code?
Clean code is code organized so tha
t its purpose is clear and its responsibilities are separated. Meaningful names and focused methods make the program easier to understand and maintain.
6. Why should a large amount of unrelated logic not be placed inside one method?
A method containing too

many unrelated instructions becomes difficult to understand and maintain. Separate methods should be created for separate responsibilities, such as accepting input, calculating an area, and displaying the result.
7. What is the purpose of an acceptInput()
method in a shape class?
The acceptInput() method obtains the values required by that shape. For example, a square needs its side, a rectangle needs its length and breadth, and a circle needs its radius.
8. Why should input-handling logic be separated fro
m area-calculation logic?
Separating input from calculation gives each method a clear responsibility. The input method obtains the required dimensions, while the calculation method performs the mathematical operation.
9. What is the purpose of a
calculateArea() method?
The calculateArea() method performs the formula required for the particular shape and returns the calculated area.
10. What is the purpose of a displayArea() method?
The displayArea() method displays the calculated area so that the
result can be seen by the user.
11. Which property is required to calculate the area of a square?
A square requires its side length. The area is calculated by multiplying the side length by itself.
12. What is the formula for calculating the area of a squa
re?
The formula is side × side, or side².
For example, if the side is 5, the area is 5 × 5 = 25.
13. Which properties are required to calculate the area of a rectangle?
A rectangle requires its length and breadth. Both values are obtained as input before
calculating the area.
14. What is the formula for calculating the area of a rectangle?
The formula is length × breadth.
For example, if the length is 4 and the breadth is 6, the area is 4 × 6 = 24.
15. Which property is required to calculate the area of a
circle?
A circle requires its radius. The radius is used in the area formula.
16. What is the formula for calculating the area of a circle?
The formula is π × radius × radius, or πr². The value of π can be approximated as 3.14 or 22/7.
17. Why is π treate
d as a constant when calculating the area of a circle?
π is a fixed mathematical value used in the circle-area formula. The formula combines this constant with the square of the radius.
18. How can keyboard input be accepted in Java?
The Scanner class can
be used to read keyboard input. A Scanner object can be created using System.in, which represents the standard input stream.
19. What does System.in represent in a Scanner declaration?
System.in represents the standard input stream, which is commonly used
to read input entered through the keyboard.
20. Why should input, calculation, and display be handled by separate methods?
Separating these responsibilities makes the code easier to follow. Each method performs a specific task, so changes to input handling
do not require rewriting the area-calculation logic.
21. What is the difference between a class property and a class behavior?
A property represents the data or state maintained by an object, such as the side of a square or the radius of a circle. A
behavior represents an operation the object can perform, such as accepting input or calculating its area.
22. How does encapsulation apply to the shape-area application?
Encapsulation keeps an object's data inside its class and controls how that data is
accessed or changed. Shape dimensions can be kept private and used through the class's methods.
23. Why are shape dimensions declared as private fields in an encapsulated design?
Private fields prevent unrelated code from directly changing the object's int
ernal data. The class can control how values are accepted and used.
24. What is inheritance in Java?
Inheritance allows one class to acquire and extend the members of another class. It helps related classes share a common structure while providing their ow
n specialized behavior.
25. How can inheritance be represented in the shape-area application?
A common parent class named Shape can be used as the base type, while Square, Rectangle, and Circle extend Shape. Each child class supplies the behavior needed fo
r its own dimensions and area calculation.
26. How does abstraction apply to a Shape parent class?
A Shape parent class can define the common operations expected from every shape, while leaving shape-specific area calculation to its subclasses. This lets t
he program work with the general concept of a shape without depending on one particular formula.
27. What is method overriding in the shape-area application?
Method overriding occurs when a child class provides its own implementation of a method declared i
n the parent class. Square, Rectangle, and Circle can each implement calculateArea() using their own formula.
28. How does polymorphism help when working with Square, Rectangle, and Circle objects?
Polymorphism allows a parent-class reference such as Shape
to refer to objects of different child classes. Calling an overridden method through that reference executes the implementation belonging to the actual object.
29. What is the benefit of using a Shape reference instead of writing separate handling code fo
r every shape?
A common Shape reference allows different shape objects to be handled through the same type. The program can call the shared operations while each object performs its own area calculation.
30. Write a Java program that calculates the areas o
f a square, rectangle, and circle using an object-oriented design.
The program uses an abstract Shape class and three child classes. Each child class accepts its required dimensions and overrides calculateArea(). A Shape reference is used to process all th
ree objects.
Sample Input
Square side: 5
Rectangle length: 4
Rectangle breadth: 6
Circle radius: 3
Sample Output:
Square area: 25.00
Rectangle area: 24.00
Circle area: 28.26
